label: run1

environment.postgresql: PostgreSQL 16.12 on x86_64-pc-linux-musl, compiled by gcc (Alpine 15.2.0) 15.2.0, 64-bit
environment.transport: brant-api process on 127.0.0.1, HTTP/1.1 keep-alive, JSON
environment.identity: local OIDC issuer of the load generator (RS256, typ at+jwt, JWKS by discovery)

workload: BRC-001 on one tenant and company (company.A), one customer (customer.1), one RFQ (rfq.1, 4 lines, 120 PCS) and one cost snapshot (660.00 USD). A command user repeats the order cycle: evd file.register (the customer's PO, ~3.7 KiB text), trd quote.save_draft, quote.freeze, GET quote, quote.submit_review, quote.review.decide, quote.activate (formal document and QT number), evd source.register (the customer's mail), quote.response.record, quote.response.verify, order.prepare, GET order, order.review.request, order.review.decide, cnx trade_compliance.evaluate, GET check, trade_compliance.decide, stl credit.reserve (672.00 of the shared customer credit), GET order check, trd order.activate, pur purchase.draft.prepare (600.00): 17 commands and 4 reads, as six humans (sales, quote.reviewer, acceptance.verifier, order.reviewer, compliance, purchaser). A read user issues one of 14 GET routes uniformly on the cycles completed so far. Closed loop, no think time; brant-worker -dispatch relays the Outbox to the contexts' consumers (STL consumes the reservation on OrderActivated).
not_executed: a front end: latencies are client-side over loopback HTTP (server plus transport), not browser end to end
a real identity provider: tokens come from the load generator's local issuer (RS256, at+jwt); each actor's token is reused for 7.5 minutes
several tenants or customers: every user works in one tenant on one customer, so the shared rows (POL quote number sequence, STL customer credit, authority guard) are contended as hard as possible
AI tasks, large reports, files above 4 KiB and external services: baseline 11.1 sets their limits apart
failures (process restart, database interruption, redelivery) during the stages: the recovery drill covers the database
a production-like host: the API, the worker, PostgreSQL (Docker) and the load generator share one WSL2 host with other work
